svg.title: NIC load balancing based on Node 0, CP ranks 0 through 7, in the supplied Magi MSA CP32 plot
svg.desc: Source: Clipboard_Screenshot_1788424789.png, identical to the README workload image cp32_shared_kv_prefixes_9_docs.png. Magi MSA CP32 min_heap, CSV row 1, sample_id 1, chunk 512, 196608 tokens and nine sequences. The orange Forward remote TX bars for ranks 0 through 7 are estimated at 82.6, 64.9, 60.3, 96.8, 73.2, 53.5, 89.6, and 111.1 MB, rounded to 0.1 MB. Their sum is approximately 632.0 MB and the ideal node-local mean is 79.0 MB per sender. Reassigning 64.1 MB locally balances the modeled send queues. The source excludes self-copy but does not separate intra-node and inter-node TX; this is a per-NIC load model derived from those bars, not measured NIC traffic or measured optimized results. Equal-bandwidth ideal network-phase time changes from 111.1/B to 79.0/B, before adding redistribution and routing overhead.
svg.text: NIC load balancing for Node 0 · CP ranks 0–7
Source: orange Forward remote TX bars • CSV row 1 / sample_id 1 • read from the supplied plot
Proposed balance; optimized values are not measured.
Same modeled total, evenly shared across all eight NICs.
Preserve token identities and destinations; use the Node 0 mean, not the 32-rank mean.
Time = payload / B. Equal NIC bandwidth B (MB/s); no shared network bottleneck.
Idle while other NICs are still transmitting
Redistribution and routing time must be added
Network-phase reduction in this model: ≈ 28.9%. Total time also includes D2D and routing overhead.
Source metric: Forward remote TX, excluding self-copy. The source does not separate intra-node from inter-node bytes.
These source-derived volumes model one sending NIC per rank; they are not direct NIC counters or measured optimized results.
Source image: Magi MSA CP32 min_heap · CSV row 1 / sample_id 1 · chunk 512 · 196,608 tokens · 9 documents.
